overview: White plays the queen to e2 instead of 2.d4, supporting e4 and avoiding the French main lines. Black usually replies 2...c5 or 2...d5 with an easy game, since the queen blocks the f1-bishop. It is a quiet, slow sideline where White aims for a flexible centre with Nf3, g3 and Bg2.

white_ideas.idea: Keep e4 solid with Qe2 and play Nf3, g3 and Bg2 for a flexible set-up.
Play d4 later when Black has committed, or meet ...c5 with Nf3 and g3.

black_ideas.idea: Strike in the centre with ...c5 and ...Nc6 followed by ...d5.
Play ...d5 at once and exploit the queen on e2 blocking the bishop.

typical_structures.structure: Sicilian-like structure after ...c5 or French pawn centre after ...d5.

character.notes: Quiet development with no forcing play.

soundness.notes: Sound but gives Black an easy game.

structure.notes: Centre not yet settled; White's d4 undecided.

level.notes: Simple ideas, not worth a repertoire.

character.reason: Quiet sideline, neither forcing nor especially solid.

level.reason: Easy ideas but not a first repertoire.

plans.reason: The queen comes out early to support e4.
